reviews.review:
After a couple more hours gameplay, I'm going to update my review, but leave my original below for initial impressions.

I am changing this to a "not recommend". I gave this one a legitimate shot, but the more I played it the more I realized it isn't just hard, it can be impossible. Even if you play perfectly, you can lose because the game gave you a random bad seed.

The way this game works is you start on a planet, you do your thing to meet its objective, then you fly to the next planet and do it again on a new objective. You might get a good seed on the first planet, play it perfectly, then fly to the next planet with a seed that just gives you no resources. Or resources so far away from your base that you can't possibly move them fast enough. Or some but not all resources you need. It's all random. If you fail because of a bad seed, not only do you lose the second planet, you lose the first planet too. And just to add insult to injury, you also can't build up resources from planet one to bring to planet two. You always start a new planet with the bare minimum, which 9 times out of 10 isn't enough to get your footing before you fail.

I still actually really like this game. I think it's charming and would be a really fun chill resource management game, if it wasn't so completely unforgiving. I gave it my best, but I'm out.

---

Original review:
I could very easily call this a "not recommend" but I'm gonna go with recommend because I think it's more good than bad. But I think you have to know what you're getting yourself into.

It's clearly missing some QOL, that's fine, you kinda don't expect that for a dollar game. But the mechanics are there, and it works. It's fairly simple in terms of complexity, but holy cats is it unforgiving when it comes to game difficulty.

It's incredibly easy to fail right off the bat. And by fail, I mean game over. It isn't just a matter of your game slowing down or your people dying off or regressing in terms of advancement. No, if you run out of food or water for more than 2 seconds, the whole game is done and you have to start over.

You'd think that would only apply at the beginning, but as you start scaling up it can be difficult to tell if you've scaled up enough in time. If you misjudge it, you've gone terminal and won't have time to add what you need and get it functional before you run out. The very real prospect of losing all your progress at any given moment makes this one somewhat difficult to enjoy.

Oh and the music sucks, lol.

But the rest of it is actually pretty well done and I could see this one being a fun idle builder if the devs properly balanced the difficulty. 

As long as you know going into it that it's an incredibly simple, but incredibly difficult game, I think you could enjoy it.
